title: French Manga, Comic Creator Frédéric Boilet Dies at 66
content:
Boilet was born in 1960 at Épinal in Eastern France. He began his comic career with La Nuit des Archées in 1983. He then drew Le rayon vert in 1987 and 36 15 Alexia in 1990. He collaborated with writer Peeters on several works, such as Love Hotel , Tôkyô est mon jardin , and Demi-tour .

Boilet moved to Japan in 1993. He was the winner of Kodansha 's first Morning Manga Fellowship, and he began writing for manga magazines in the late 90s. He drew the Yukiko's Spinach manga in 2000-2001, which Fanfare / Ponent Mon released in English. He also drew the Mariko Parade manga with Kan Takahama in 2003. Fanfare / Ponent Mon also released that manga in English.

He conceived and contributed to the Japan as Viewed by 17 Creators anthology, which Fanfare / Ponent Mon also released in English. The anthology won a Special Award from the Japan Cartoonists Association.

Boilet adapted Jiro Taniguchi 's A Distant Neighborhood , Taniguchi and Ryuichiro Utsumi 's Keyaki no Ki , and Yoshiharu Tsuge 's Munō no Hito manga into French. He also translated comics into Japanese. He moved back to France in 2008.

title: Big Shonen Jump Hit Confirms It Will End After 6 Years With Next Release
content:
One of the biggest hits to come out of the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has now revealed it’s set to end after six years of serialization with its final chapter coming very soon. It’s been a rollercoaster of a year for Shonen Jump as there have been a number of longer running series coming to their respective ends, and a number of titles that had been cancelled shortly into their runs without any real hope of finding an audience. But it’s time to say goodbye to another series.

There have been five longer running titles that have come to an end with Shonen Jump through the year thus far , and now Yuto Suzuki’s Sakamoto Days has confirmed that it will be coming to an end with the release of its final chapter next week. This will mark a total of six years of serialization within Shonen Jump , and will be an end to one of the longer running series in the magazine of the early 2020s era. So it’s time to say goodbye before the end comes.

Sakamato Days to End After 6 Years in Shonen Jump With Chapter 284

Sakamoto Days has been circling its end for quite a while now, and that’s all going to be set with Chapter 284 coming this Sunday, November 22nd. The final arc of Yuto Suzuki’s manga originally began late last year as Taro Sakamoto and the others needed to deal with X and the destruction of the former assassination system . It’s been one intense final fight after another, and it all seemed to be wrapping up with its latest chapters. This seemed to be even more the case with Chapter 282 as Sakamoto was able to deal the final blow to X and end the fight once and for all.

Sakamoto Days’ penultimate chapter (Chapter 283) then picks up a year after the fight with X , and reveals that Sakamoto has since opened up even more of his convenience stores all over Japan in that time (just like he dreamed he would). Revealing how Japan has basically returned to peace after all that time, Sakamoto and the others have been working hard to maintain it. But as it gears up for its finale, Sakamoto’s daughter Hana has been kidnapped and it has sparked one final adventure to go out on.

What Does This Mean for Shonen Jump ‘s Future?

The end of Sakamoto Days comes just a week after Kenta Shinohara’s Witch Watch released its own final chapter after a five year long run . This marks another two of the longer running hits from Shonen Jump coming to an end one after another, and puts one more nail in the coffin of the late 2010s-early 2020s generation of titles. This will also be the sixth series to reach its respective conclusion with the magazine this year after Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo, Hima-ten!, Blue Box and The Elusive Samurai before it.

There are three new titles coming to Shonen Jump through the rest of the month with the first, Jan Is in Danger! , making its own debut this week . That means two replacements are set with Sakamoto Days getting its own replacement soon, and it likely means another title is going to end next week. It’s likely going to be a cancellation, however, as nothing else seems ready to end by its own terms right now. But how do you feel about Sakamoto Days ending after six years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Black Clover Season 2 Next Episode First Look Kicks Off Final Dark Triad Fight
content:
Black Clover is kicking off the final fight against the Dark Triad in full with the first look at what’s coming next in Season 2’s next big episode. Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the Spade Kingdom Raid arc from Yuki Tabata’s original manga, and with it fans have gotten to see some of the biggest moments that have ever made it to the anime to date . But it’s far from over as their are still some big fights needing to settle soon.

Black Clover Season 2 has now ended the fights against Dante and Vanica with its episodes thus far , and the first look at the next episode is finally diving into the fight against the final of the siblings, Zenon Zogratis. While fans had previously seen a bit of this fight in a previous episode, it’s now going to get the main focus as teased with the first look preview images and synopsis for Black Clover Season 2 Episode 8. Check them out in the gallery below.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 8 Release Date & Synopsis Revealed

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 8 is titled “The Devil’s Heart,” and will be making its debut in Japan on November 21st, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it hits for fans in North America and other international territories. When we had last seen Yuno and Langris in action, the two of them have been going against Zenon. And that’s what the synopsis gets right into, “Yuno and Langris faced off against Zenon, who had unleashed 100% of his demonic power. Even using magic within Zenon’s spatial magic was difficult for ordinary mages…”

But while this fight against Zenon has been rough thus far, it seems like Langris is going to play a big role in Yuno’s big move against the Dark Triad sibling , “But then Langris, the strongest spatial mage in the Clover Kingdom, reached the mana zone and unleashed his full power!” the synopsis reads. But while it seemed like they were near victory, yet another twist takes place, “With Langris’s support, Yuno’s Spirit of Euros finally pierced Zenon’s body. Yuno was convinced that victory was near, but Zenon’s demeanor suddenly changed after he made a deal with the demon Beelzebub—!?”

What’s Next for Black Clover Season 2?

Black Clover has seen the Clover Kingdom Knights needing to stop the members of the Dark Triad in order to interrupt the Advent of Qliphoth ritual before Yami and Vangeance are sacrificed, and two members of the Dark Triad and their demonic partners has been stopped thus far. But even with that happening, there have been some of the Supreme Devils that have been able to make it through the cracks to wreak havoc on everyone . So it remains to be seen what’s next.

At the rate Black Clover Season 2 has been going thus far, it’s likely that the Spade Kingdom Raid arc will be wrapping up its run by the end of the season. That’s only going to be a few more episodes from this point , so it remains to be seen how the series is going to then adapt the final arc to come. But how are you liking Black Clover Season 2 so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: The Days of Diamond Manga Gets TV Anime
content:
A new official website opened on Tuesday to announce that Ōhashi Hirai 's The Days of Diamond ( Diamond no Kōzai ) manga is getting a television anime. The website revealed a visual and the main staff:

Series creator Hirai drew an illustration to commemorate the announcement:

Takakazu Nagatomo ( You and I Are Polar Opposites ) is directing the anime at Lapin Track . Chigusa Kiyota (episode director for Delicious in Dungeon ) is the assistant director. Atsushi Saitо̄ ( Love Live! Superstar!! ) is designing the characters. Teruko Utsumi ( Eiga Doraemon: Nobita no Chikyū Symphony ) is handling the series composition and screenplay. Kumiko Yanagisawa ( Draw This, Then Die! ) is in charge of color design. Hisako Akagi ( Campfire Cooking in Another World with My Absurd Skill ) is the art director.

“I was meant to play baseball!” Jiro Ayasegawa has a natural gift for sports, but life can be lonely at the top. He's crushed other players' dreams. Some have even given up their sport altogether because of him. Eventually, he encounters "The Bambies," a low-level, local kids' baseball team that plays purely for fun. Jiro signs up, thinking that he's finally found an easy-going team to enjoy baseball with, until things take a sudden turn...

Hirai launched the manga in Shueisha 's Young Jump magazine in February 2023. Shueisha published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on November 18.

The series most recently returned on June 4 from a hiatus that started on January 22. Prior to that, the manga returned from hiatus in September 2025. The manga went on an earlier hiatus on September 5, 2024 due to Hirai preparing to release the seventh compiled book volume. The manga was originally slated to resume on October 3, 2024, before delaying the return to October 31, 2024. The manga previously went on hiatus in August 2024 due to personal reasons for Hirai, and returned at the end of that month.

title: Manga 'Diamond no Kouzai' Gets TV Anime
content:
Production company TOHO animation opened an official website for a television anime adaptation of Oohashi Hirai 's Diamond no Kouzai ( The Days of Diamond ) manga on Tuesday, revealing the main staff and an announcement visual (pictured).

Staff Director: Takakazu Nagatomo ( Seihantai na Kimi to Boku ) Assistant Director: Chigusa Kiyota ( Dungeon Meshi episode director) Series Composition, Script: Teruko Utsumi ( Nippon Sangoku ) Character Design: Atsushi Saitou ( Shoushimin Series ) Color Design: Kumiko Yanagizawa ( Boku no Kokoro no Yabai Yatsu ) Art Director: Hisako Akagi ( Tondemo Skill de Isekai Hourou Meshi ) Studio: Lapin Track

Hirai began serializing the coming-of-age sports manga in Young Jump since February 2023. Shueisha published the tenth volume on July 17, with the 11th volume scheduled for a November 18 release. Diamond no Kouzai has over 2 million copies in circulation.

Shueisha has simulpublished the manga digitally in English through their Manga Plus platform since February 2024.

Diamond no Kouzai placed seventh in the print category of the 2023 Next Manga Awards and placed first in the male readers category of the Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2024 rankings. The series also placed fifth in the 2024 Manga Taisho Awards .

Synopsis "I was meant to play baseball!" Jirou Ayasegawa has a natural gift for sports, but life can be lonely at the top. He's crushed other players' dreams. Some have even given up their sport altogether because of him. Eventually, he encounters "The Bambies," a low-level, local kids' baseball team that plays purely for fun. Jirou signs up, thinking that he's finally found an easy-going team to enjoy baseball with, until things take a sudden turn... (Source: MANGA Plus)

title: OceanVeil Streams English Dub for Hands Off: Sawaranaide Koteashi-kun Anime
content:
The English dub cast includes:

• Brittany Lauda as Aroma Kusunoki

• Sean Flaherty as Koyo Kotesashi

• Kira Buckland as Chiyo Sayamagaoka

• Betty BAT as Miyuki Hongo

• Diana Garnet as Izumi Sumiyoshi

• Leah Booth as Aoba Kitahara

• Angel Haven Rey as Vice Principal

• P.M. Seymour as Coach Sakamoto

• Steve Warky Nunez as Izumi's Dad

The English dub staff includes:

• Executive Producer: Jonathan Hinga

• ADR Director: P.M. Seymour

• ADR Assistant Director: Zack Maher

• Production Assistant: Amanda Parker

• Time Coding: Jasper Bear

• ADR Engineers: Jack T. Westlake / Zack Maher, Andrea Stewart

• Mix Engineer / Mastering: Steve Warky Nunez

• Adaptation: Laura K. Welsh

• Localization Supervisor: Kevin Frane

• Talent Sourcing: No Studio In Particular (Reece Bridger)

• Public Relations: Paul Davey

• Marketing: Mana T. Johnson

• Quality Assurance: Shane Tay / Brian Rollins

• Subtitles: Danny Miller / L.L.

The anime debuted in October 2025. A "Complete Deregula Version" is streaming on AnimeFesta that is uncensored. The partially censored " Deregula Version" and the censored broadcast version are also streaming on AnimeFesta and other streaming services.

OceanVeil is also streaming the anime's uncensored version with English subtitles.

Hisashi Saitō ( I’m Living with an Otaku NEET Kunoichi!? , Fantasista Doll ) directed the anime at Quad . Gokō Shiraki was in charge of series scripts, Ryūsuke Tsukamoto ( The Apothecary Diaries , Protocol: Rain animation director) designed the characters, and Chihiro Endō composed the music. Deregula produced the anime.

Additional staff includes:

• Color Design: Daiki Ura

• Art Director: Makoto Shiraishi

• Compositing Director of Photography: Makoto Tōgō

• Editing: Jun'ichi Masunaga

• Sound Director: Kōhei Yoshida

UtaGe! performed the opening theme song "U.K.U," and Palette Parade performed the ending theme song "Jōjō ↑ High Tension."

OceanVeil describes the series:

"Devote yourself to physical and mental care, Dorm Caretaker Kotesashi!" Koyo Kotesashi is a high school freshman with a special skill: giving super massages that feel way too good! In order to earn his tuition fee and secure a scholarship for medical school, Koyo becomes a live-in dorm manager at a prestigious sports school, Seiwa University High School. There he meets an erratic bunch of eccentric but stunningly beautiful athlete girls! In order to secure his special scholarship, Koyo devotes himself to providing the girls with physical and mental care. Too much to bare or too precious to bare? It is too heavy-handed, yet too heavenly…!? Here's a fresh new massage rom-com that will leave you writhing with delight!!

Shinjō launched the manga in Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket app in May 2021.

title: Dragon Ball Super Remake Wraps Battle of Gods Arc With Epic Finale Fight
content:
Dragon Ball Super ‘s big remake anime series has now reached the end of the Battle of Gods arc with its latest episode, and fans got a newly enhanced version of the final fight with Beerus as a result. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus introduced a new enhanced version of the now classic Dragon Ball Super TV anime starting with the Battle of Gods arc, and the episodes thus far have seen how this new series has retooled the classic episodes to deliver a mostly new experience .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has now wrapped up the Battle of Gods arc with Episode 6 of the new anime series, and it has already been a much more streamlined experience than the classic TV series. Getting to the end of the fight against Beerus in a much quicker fashion , the final moments of the fight also featured some visual upgrades that make it stand out much more than the classic series (as spotted by @DBPerfectShots on X ). Naturally, opening up a debate about which version has been the best thus far.

Dragon Ball Super Ends the Battle of Gods Arc for the Third Time

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 6 has officially ended the Battle of Gods arc , and with it marks the third anime iteration of this major arc following its original movie and TV anime versions. Each version of the arc has notably been different from one another, and the remake further adjusts things for its own take. One notable difference from the original TV version is Goku’s final moments before his defeat as he smiles a bit before crashing down on Earth. And it’s an adjustment that’s very much welcome.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been making a number of adjustments to the original TV anime, but unfortunately it’s been reusing the audio from that original series for the occasion. It’s meant that this new remake won’t be changing as much as fans might want it to from the original (especially those who were hoping for additional materials from the manga release), but at least it’s been able to adjust its visuals enough to make it truly feel like a new enough experience for those who haven’t revisited that older anime in quite some time.

What’s Next for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ?

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus thankfully will keep going with its remake anime series despite being named after the God of Destruction himself. It has been confirmed that this new series will also be showcasing new versions of the Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs , and Resurrection F will begin in full with the next episode. This does raise a lot of questions as this arc has been a bumpy experience with both its original film and TV releases, so this is going to be the real test for the remake.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has yet to confirm how many episodes it will be running for, but it’s likely going to go beyond the end of the Fall 2026 anime schedule . This first arc took six episodes to get through, and the next two arcs won’t likely wrap up within the next six or seven weeks before the Fall ends. That means we’ll likely see the remake continue through to next Winter, but its future from then on is uncertain.

How did you like this new version of the Battle of Gods arc in Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ? Did it change enough from the original TV anime for you? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus introduced a new enhanced version of the now classic Dragon Ball Super TV anime starting with the Battle of Gods arc, and the episodes thus far have seen how this new series has retooled the classic episodes to deliver a mostly new experience .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has now wrapped up the Battle of Gods arc with Episode 6 of the new anime series, and it has already been a much more streamlined experience than the classic TV series. Getting to the end of the fight against Beerus in a much quicker fashion , the final moments of the fight also featured some visual upgrades that make it stand out much more than the classic series (as spotted by @DBPerfectShots on X ). Naturally, opening up a debate about which version has been the best thus far.
Dragon Ball Super Ends the Battle of Gods Arc for the Third Time

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 6 has officially ended the Battle of Gods arc , and with it marks the third anime iteration of this major arc following its original movie and TV anime versions. Each version of the arc has notably been different from one another, and the remake further adjusts things for its own take. One notable difference from the original TV version is Goku’s final moments before his defeat as he smiles a bit before crashing down on Earth. And it’s an adjustment that’s very much welcome.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been making a number of adjustments to the original TV anime, but unfortunately it’s been reusing the audio from that original series for the occasion. It’s meant that this new remake won’t be changing as much as fans might want it to from the original (especially those who were hoping for additional materials from the manga release), but at least it’s been able to adjust its visuals enough to make it truly feel like a new enough experience for those who haven’t revisited that older anime in quite some time.
What’s Next for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ?

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus thankfully will keep going with its remake anime series despite being named after the God of Destruction himself. It has been confirmed that this new series will also be showcasing new versions of the Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs , and Resurrection F will begin in full with the next episode. This does raise a lot of questions as this arc has been a bumpy experience with both its original film and TV releases, so this is going to be the real test for the remake.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has yet to confirm how many episodes it will be running for, but it’s likely going to go beyond the end of the Fall 2026 anime schedule . This first arc took six episodes to get through, and the next two arcs won’t likely wrap up within the next six or seven weeks before the Fall ends. That means we’ll likely see the remake continue through to next Winter, but its future from then on is uncertain.

How did you like this new version of the Battle of Gods arc in Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ? Did it change enough from the original TV anime for you? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: 34% of Developers in 2026 GDC Survey Were Laid Off in Last 2 Years
content:
The Game Developers Conference (GDC) released the results of its 15th annual "State of the Game Industry Survey" last Thursday and revealed that 34% of game developers surveyed were laid off in the last 24 months, up from 28% last year. Of that 34%, 68% stated they were laid off in the last 12 months. 49% of those surveyed reported that their company conducted layoffs in some form in the past 12 months.

54% of those laid off have not found new employment. Of those who have found new employment, 9% of have left the game industry, while 4% have their own game industry companies.

40% of game developers report using generative AI in their work, with 57% of those stating they use it daily. However, usage remains polarizing, with 55% of developers saying it has a negative impact on games. Mobile-only developers and developers working on free-to-play games report the highest usage at 70% and 58%, respectively. 27% of workers from AAA studios report being encouraged or pressured to use generative AI, with only 9% of indie studio workers reporting the same.

The survey noted of those who use AI tools as part of their job, 38% from the U.S. stated they did, and 44% outside of the U.S. stated they did.

35% of developers are using Unreal Engine to develop their game, being the most popular engine among respondents, but down from 42% last year. Unity is the second most popular engine, with 28% of developers using the engine, down from 30% last year. 23% of developers report using proprietary or in-house engines.

86% of responses report more fulfilment working in the game industry compared to other industries, though 86% of developers also report working more than 40 hours in a single week over the past year, with 46% reporting working more than 40 hours a week on average. 66% of respondents see working in the game industry as part of their identity and self-worth. 65% say their mental health has suffered due to their game industry job, but only looking at those who are currently unemployed, the percentage jumps to 81%.

80% of respondents in the United States support unionization of game industry workers, while 55% are interested in joining a union. 20% are not currently in a union and are not seeking to join one.

81% of developers are working on games for the PC, with 45% developing for PlayStation 5, 37% developing for Xbox Series X|S, 32% developing for Steam Deck, and 29% developing for Nintendo Switch 2 (overlap can exist as games often release on multiple platforms). 10% of respondents are developing games for the upcoming next generation PlayStation console, while 8% are developing for Xbox's upcoming "Project Helix" device.

46% of developers report an interest in developing for the Switch 2, up from 37% last year, while 38% report interest in developing games built for the Steam Deck (games developer for Steam Deck are also PC games by definition).

The survey asked more than 2,600 game developers about their work and about the industry. 63% of respondents live in the United States, and 3% live in Japan.

The Game Developers Conference will be held at the Moscone Convention Center in San Francisco from March 1 through March 4.

title: The Summer Hikaru Died Novels End With 3rd Volume
content:
Yen Press is releasing the novels in English, and it describes the story:

The bond between Yoshiki and Hikaru is a welcome escape from their isolated village. But one day when the two boys meet up, Yoshiki can immediately tell something is off. Though the person standing before him looks and acts exactly like Hikaru, Yoshiki knows that his friend is... gone. Someone―no, something has taken Hikaru's place. And with so many eerie incidents happening in town lately, Yoshiki is becoming increasingly conflicted. Although things will never be as they once were, he would prefer this Hikaru to no Hikaru at all.

Nukaga launched the novel series with the first volume in December 2023. The second volume shipped in Japan in July 2025. Yen Press released the first novel volume in English in April 2025.

Mokumokuren launched the manga on Kadokawa 's Young Ace Up website in August 2021, and ended it on October 20. Kadokawa published the manga's ninth compiled book volume on June 4, and will publish the 10th and final volume on January 25. The manga exceeded 3 million copies in circulation by the time of the sixth volume's release.

Yen Press publishes the manga in English, and released the manga's eighth volume on October 27.

The manga was nominated for the 16th Manga Taisho Awards. (The official English name of the awards is the "Cartoon Grand Prize.") The New York Public Library listed the manga as part of its Best Books list for teens in 2023. The manga also made The American Library Association's (ALA's) Young Adult Library Services Association (YALSA) 2024 list of Great Graphic Novels for Teens.

Both the manga and its author Mokumokuren were nominated for the Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards in 2024. The manga was nominated for the Best U.S. Edition of International Material—Asia category, while Mokumokuren was nominated for the Best Writer/Artist category.

The manga's anime adaptation debuted in July 2025. The anime will have a second season.

The manga also inspired a stage play adaptation that ran from January 9-18 at Kinokuniya Hall in Tokyo.

title: Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? Anime Unveils Main Visual
content:
A main visual was unveiled for the upcoming Are You a Landmine, Chihara-san? anime. Studio SynergySP is animating the series with Yasuaki Fujii as director. It is set to premiere on January 7, 2027.

A teaser trailer was previously released. Keiichiro Ochi is in charge of the series composition while Majiro is on character designs, and Alisa Okehazama is composing the music. The main voice cast consists of:

• Sayumi Suzushiro as Mai Chihara

• Kazuki Ura as Kuroki

• Maaya Uchida as Chinatsu Iwakura

• Tomokazu Sugita as Hibiya

• Daisuke Ono as Kazami

Ryon launched the manga on Comic Smart’s Ganma! website in June 2021 and currently has 8 volumes in circulation. Seven Seas will release the mang in English on September 29, 2026. They describe it as follows: Don’t judge a book by its cover or a girl by her fashion taste! A slice-of-life rom-com manga about wrong impressions and looking beyond appearances. The manga that inspired the upcoming anime It’s the start of a new semester, and high school junior Kuroki finds himself seated beside the girl everyone whispers about: Mai Chihara. With her gothic fashion, jet-black hair, and intense stare, Chihara is said to be a “landmine” girl or jirai-kei, the hyper-feminine, dark aesthetic often associated with yandere tendencies and unstable personalities. But when Kuroki accidentally draws Chihara’s attention, he discovers she isn’t nearly as unstable as people claim. Beneath the intimidating aura is a surprisingly sweet girl… if a little weird. Hesitantly, Kuroki begins to learn more about Chihara and her strange quirks. Is there more to her than her volatile reputation? Or is all the dark clothing just a red flag in disguise?
